problems.form_value: treatment_arm Variation(1) in both contrasts. The notes say Appendices C and E label the AI arm 'Variation' and the form reads it as Variation(1). statistics_available arm_means_sds_ns.
problems.source_says: Appendix E never says which Variation arm it uses, and the Section 4.1 label holds only 'in this section'. The arithmetic of Table E.2 points to a pooled column. 'Vertical layout present' is a binary scene-graph feature (Table WA-B.1). Its share in the Variation submission column, 0.964, cannot be k/575 (554/575 = 0.963, 555/575 = 0.965). It fits Variation(1) plus Variation(4): 1,084 or 1,085 of 1,125. The other seven Variation shares also fit 1,125, and Variation(4) alone (550) fails three of them. The Open (470/499) and Blind (502/575) shares fit their own counts, so missing values are an unlikely cause. The exemplar Variation share, 0.963, cannot be k/60 but equals 231/240, the four-per-exemplar set of Web Appendix B.3. So Table E.2 most likely pools both AI arms, and Table E.3, from the same analysis, probably does too. The arm should read 'Variation (not stated; likely Variation(1) and Variation(4) pooled)'. The All Submissions N is then 575 or 1,125. Table E.3 prints no N, so arm_means_sds_ns should say the Ns are derived. No coded direction changes.

problems.form_value: No fluency outcome. The notes name only the refinement comparison and the model-only validation studies as not coded.
problems.source_says: Appendix B reports designs submitted per participating designer (7.5 on average) and says pairwise t-tests found no significant difference across conditions. Section 4.1 calls this 'submission depth'. Table 1 prints submissions and participating designers by arm: Variation(1) 575 and 71, Blind 575 and 75, Open 499 and 70, Variation(4) 550 and 76. The codebook defines fluency as the number of ideas a person produces. The count is a post-treatment outcome produced while the gallery was open, so it bears on with_ai. The paper treats it as a participation check, it covers only designers who submitted, and no arm mean, SD, or p-value is printed. The form should code it as a secondary fluency outcome (category_count, unit participant, no_clear_difference) or say in notes why it is left out. Study 2 has the same gap: Section 5 says participation did not differ, and Table 2 gives Variation 367 and 64, Blind 341 and 79, Open 319 and 65.

problems.form_value: Footnote 2 says the ratings come from an online survey similar to Section 3.2.2 (respondents choose which logo of a pair they would click in an online ad) and that submissions are benchmarked against the original brief exemplars.
problems.source_says: Footnote 2 is attached to the in-contest feedback: each day the researchers rated 10 randomly sampled new submissions per condition and sent the ratings privately to their designers. It says how those feedback ratings were collected. It does not describe the outcome that scores all 2,199 submissions. The paper describes the outcome only as 'survey-based ratings on how well logos attract clicks in online ads', and for Study 2 as collected with 'the same method as in the main study'. The code human_raters still holds. The pairwise-survey method of the outcome is an inference, and measure_detail should label it as one.

problems.source_says: The codebook defines automated_score as 'a scoring model for creativity: semantic-distance scoring of divergent-thinking tests, or a language model used as judge'. The alignment score is the maximum, over the 12 exemplars, of a composite of Dice overlaps of motif and color sets (extracted with ChatGPT 5.2), a text-embedding similarity of motifs, color-moment and style distances, and scene-graph and Hu-moment distances (Table WA-B.2). It measures similarity to the exemplars, not creativity. No codebook measure code fits it exactly, and measure_detail should say so. This is minor: the outcome is secondary and its construct is 'other'.
problems.quote: For each submission, we compute its alignment measures with the 12 original exemplars and then take the maximum as the submission’s alignment score.
problems.locator: PDF p. 42 (printed p. 41), Appendix E.2; PDF p. 53 (WA-9), Table WA-B.2; codebook section 6, Measure

confirmed: S1-O1 and S2-O1 are computed on each submitted logo: the minimum, over the 12 leading first-page exemplars, of 1 minus the CLIP cosine similarity. This is a computed measure, not a self-report, so novelty and embedding_similarity fit. The model name comes from the LAION (2022) reference (PDF pp. 22-23, Section 4.3 and footnote 3; PDF p. 34, references; PDF p. 30, Section 5).

Quality is survey-based click attractiveness of each submitted logo, so human_raters and usefulness fit. Study 2 uses the same method (PDF p. 5, Introduction; PDF p. 24, Section 4.4; PDF pp. 65-66, Web Appendix D.2).

S1-O3: survey participants rated similarity on color, composition, and style (15 per pair and dimension, 7-point scale, two calibration pairs). The score is the minimum over leading exemplars of the mean of the three. Figure C.1 prints p = 0.024 (Open vs Variation), 0.857 (Variation vs Blind), and 0.040 (Open vs Blind), and the text prints -0.351 and 0.0257. No N is stated. Reading its 'Variation' as Variation(1) rests on Section 4.3, which sends the perception-based results to Appendix C. No arithmetic contradicts it (PDF p. 22, Section 4.3; PDF pp. 37-39, Appendix C and Figure C.1).

S1-O4 is computed on each submission as its maximum alignment with the 12 original exemplars. Every mean, SD, and Delta-vs-Blind value in the form matches Table E.3, and rho = 0.453 matches the text (PDF pp. 42-44, Appendix E.2 and Table E.3).

Galleries were assigned at the start of the two-week contest, restricted by designer ID, and visits were logged. The AI variations were open while every scored logo was produced, and no output was scored after a gallery was removed. So ai_available_when_produced yes, timing immediate, and question with_ai hold for all six outcomes, and no after_ai record is missing (PDF pp. 17-18, Section 4.1; PDF p. 23, footnote 3).

Every outcome regression runs at the submission level with designer-clustered SEs, and Table E.3 averages over submissions, so unit output holds for all six outcomes (PDF p. 23, Section 4.3; notes to Tables WA-C.1, WA-C.2, WA-D.2, WA-D.3, PDF pp. 62-63 and 67-68).

Every S1-O1 and S1-O2 coefficient, SE, and contrast matches Tables WA-C.1 to WA-C.4. The text and Figure 6 and 7 p-values (0.008, 0.516, 0.001, 0.930) reproduce from those tables (PDF pp. 23-25 and 62-64).

Figure 9 prints p = 0.543 (originality) and p = 0.918 (quality) for Variation(1) vs Variation(4). The text gives -0.003 for originality, both quality bars sit near 0.57, and the figure notes swap the panel descriptions (PDF p. 27, Section 4.5 and Figure 9).
Every S2-O1 and S2-O2 coefficient, SE, and contrast matches Tables WA-D.2 to WA-D.5. The Figure 11A p-values (0.039, 0.635) reproduce from Table WA-D.4 (PDF pp. 30 and 67-69).

n_units: 200 is the top 50 in each of four arms, and 2,199 is 499 + 575 + 550 + 575, so both include Variation(4) submissions. Study 2 uses 150 and 1,027 (PDF p. 20, Table 1; PDF pp. 62-63, WA-18 to WA-19; PDF pp. 67-68, WA-23 to WA-24).

Originality is distance to the 2019 contest exemplars, not to other participants, so novelty is right and diversity would be wrong. The paper reports no across-people diversity measure on participants' logos. Its only dispersion test covers the AI gallery itself, a model-only check (PDF p. 22, Section 4.3; PDF pp. 56-57, WA-12 to WA-13).
Blind (brief only) is ai_vs_bau, Open (human-made exemplars) is ai_vs_active, and Variation(4) vs Variation(1) is ai_design with Variation(4) as the tested configuration (PDF p. 18, Section 4.1).

Leaving out the refinement comparison (Figure 10) is defensible. It sets Variation submissions against AI variations polished by separately recruited designers, with no random assignment (PDF p. 28, Section 4.5; PDF pp. 38-39, Appendix D).
summary: Criterion 3 holds: the embedding originality and survey-rated quality of the submitted logos (S1-O1, S1-O2, and their Study 2 replications) are scored on participants' output while the assigned AI gallery was open, and question, construct, unit, AI availability, and every transcribed number check out against the PDF. The coding is refuted on details: Table E.2 arithmetic shows the Appendix E 'Variation' column most likely pools Variation(1) and Variation(4), so the Variation(1) arm of S1-O4 is unsupported, and the form also omits designs per designer (a fluency count tested in Appendix B), takes the quality method from the feedback footnote, leaves the conflict between Figure 11B and Table WA-D.5 p-values unnoted, and uses automated_score outside its codebook definition.
